subject: English
description: A/an/the rules: indefinite vs definite, zero article, with abstract/proper nouns

questions.stem: Choose the correct articles: '___ honest man is ___ asset to ___ society.'

options.option_text: A / a / a (all indefinite forms here)
An / an / Ø (no article before 'society')
The / the / the (all definite forms used)
An / a / the (mixed articles all together)

questions.explanation: 'Honest' starts with silent H (vowel sound) → 'AN honest'. 'Asset' starts with vowel → 'AN asset'. 'Society' is an abstract/general noun used in a general sense → ZERO article (Ø). Rule of articles before H: silent H takes 'an' (an hour, an honour, an honest); pronounced H takes 'a' (a hospital, a hotel, a house).

questions.stem: Pick the correct article: 'He is ___ MBA from ___ IIM Bangalore.'

options.option_text: A / the (definite for institute name)
An / Ø (no article before IIM)
The / an (mixed combo here)
An / the (definite institute too)

questions.explanation: MBA pronounced 'em-bee-ay' starts with VOWEL SOUND ('em') → AN MBA. Names of specific institutions like IIM Bangalore (when used with location) take ZERO article. (Compare: 'he is at the IIM' — generic — vs. 'he studied at IIM Bangalore' — proper noun + place). Rule for letters/abbreviations: F, H, L, M, N, R, S, X start with vowel sound → 'an' (an FIR, an MA, an X-ray).

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: '___ Ganges is ___ holiest river in India.'

options.option_text: A / a (indefinite article both)
The / the (definite for both terms)
Ø / the (only second has it)
The / a (mixed article forms)

questions.explanation: Rule 1: rivers, oceans, seas, mountain ranges take THE (the Ganges, the Nile, the Arabian Sea, the Himalayas). Rule 2: superlatives (holiest, biggest, smallest) always take THE. So 'THE Ganges' + 'THE holiest river'. Mountains as a single peak don't take 'the' (Mount Everest, Mount Fuji).

questions.stem: Choose the correct article: 'She plays ___ piano but doesn't play ___ cricket.'

options.option_text: A / a (using indefinite article both)
The / Ø (definite for instrument, none for sport)
Ø / the (zero piano, definite cricket)
The / the (definite for both terms used)

questions.explanation: Rule: musical INSTRUMENTS take THE (play THE piano, the guitar, the violin). SPORTS take ZERO article (play cricket, play football, play chess). Common SSC/banking error → using 'the' before sports. Memorize the pair: instruments WITH 'the', sports WITHOUT.

questions.stem: Fill in: '___ Mahatma Gandhi led ___ Indian freedom movement.'

options.option_text: A / an (indefinite article forms)
The / the (definite for honoured + named)
Ø / Ø (no article either spot)
An / the (mixed article combo)

questions.explanation: Rule: titles + proper nouns of fame take THE (the Mahatma, the Father of the Nation, the Iron Lady). Specific historical movements/events take THE (the Indian freedom movement, the French Revolution, the Cold War). 'Gandhi' alone takes Ø; 'THE Mahatma Gandhi' uses the title-form.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose: 'I had ___ uniform on, while waiting for ___ university bus.'

options.option_text: An / an (consonant-letter twice)
A / a (both start with 'yu' sound)
An / a (mixed article forms)
The / the (definite for both terms)

questions.explanation: 'Uniform', 'university', 'European', 'one-way' begin with the CONSONANT SOUND /yu:/ → take A (not 'an'), even though spelled with vowel U/E/O. Rule: articles depend on the SOUND not the LETTER. 'A uniform' (yu-niform) but 'An umbrella' (uh-mbrella).

questions.stem: Pick the correct article: '___ rich should help ___ poor.'

options.option_text: A / a (indefinite article for both)
The / the (adjective as plural noun)
Ø / Ø (no article needed at all)
An / the (mixed article combo here)

questions.explanation: Rule: ADJECTIVES used as PLURAL NOUNS to refer to a class take THE. 'The rich' = rich people; 'the poor' = poor people; 'the elderly', 'the deaf', 'the blind', 'the unemployed'. Acts as a generic plural — verb agrees in plural form (the rich ARE generous).

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: 'She gave ___ one-hour lecture on ___ art of public speaking at the national seminar.'

options.option_text: an one-hour lecture, the art of public speaking
a one-hour lecture, an art of public speaking
a one-hour lecture, the art of public speaking
an one-hour lecture, an art of public speaking

questions.explanation: 'One' is pronounced 'wʌn' — a consonant 'w' sound — so the article before it must be 'a', not 'an'. 'The art of public speaking' requires 'the' because 'the art of X' is a fixed collocation referring to a specific, named concept. Option A is the classic trap: students see 'o' in 'one' and wrongly apply 'an'.

questions.stem: Choose the correct pair: 'She carried ___ umbrella because ___ weather forecast had predicted heavy rain in the evening.'

options.option_text: a umbrella, a weather forecast had predicted
an umbrella, a weather forecast had predicted
an umbrella, the weather forecast had predicted
the umbrella, the weather forecast had predicted

questions.explanation: 'Umbrella' opens with a vowel sound, so 'an' is required. 'The weather forecast' takes 'the' because it refers to a specific, contextually known forecast. Option D is wrong: 'the umbrella' implies it was already introduced; Option B uses 'a weather forecast', treating something definite and specific as if it were any random forecast.

questions.stem: Fill in: 'This is ___ very book I was searching for; it is ___ only copy left in ___ entire city.'

options.option_text: the very book, an only copy, the entire city
the very book, the only copy, the entire city
a very book, the only copy, the entire city
the very book, the only copy, an entire city

questions.explanation: 'The very book' uses 'the' because 'very' here is an emphasiser that identifies a precise, specific item — not a description of quality. 'The only copy' demands 'the' since 'only' singles out a unique item, functioning like a superlative. 'The entire city' similarly requires 'the' as it modifies a known, bounded entity. Option A is wrong because 'an only' is ungrammatical — 'only' always partners with 'the'.

questions.stem: Choose the correct article pair for: 'He was appointed ___ honorary consul of ___ United Kingdom last year.'

options.option_text: a honorary consul, the United Kingdom last year
an honorary consul, the United Kingdom last year
an honorary consul, a United Kingdom last year
the honorary consul, the United Kingdom last year

questions.explanation: 'Honorary' has a silent 'h'; the first audible sound is the vowel 'ɒ', so 'an honorary' is correct — not 'a honorary'. Country names compounded with a common noun (Kingdom, States, Republic) always take 'the' (the United Kingdom, the United States). Option A, the most common error, applies 'a' to a silent-h word, confusing spelling with pronunciation.

questions.stem: Identify the correct article usage: '___ Himalayas act as ___ natural barrier separating the Indian subcontinent from Central Asia.'

options.option_text: The Himalayas, a natural barrier between regions
The Himalayas, the natural barrier between regions
A Himalayas, a natural barrier between regions
Himalayas, the natural barrier between the regions

questions.explanation: Named mountain ranges always take 'the' (the Himalayas, the Alps, the Rockies). 'A natural barrier' is correct because the Himalayas are one of several natural barriers on Earth — using 'the' would falsely imply they are the only such barrier. Option D omits 'the' before Himalayas, which is always incorrect for named geographical ranges.

questions.stem: Fill in: 'It is ___ pity that ___ committee overlooked ___ most qualified candidate for ___ post of director.'

options.option_text: a pity, the committee, the most qualified, the post
a pity, the committee, a most qualified, the post
the pity, a committee, the most qualified, the post
a pity, the committee, the most qualified, a post

questions.explanation: 'A pity' is a frozen idiomatic expression — 'the pity' is not used in this structure, eliminating C. 'The committee' takes 'the' as it refers to a specific, known body. Superlatives require 'the' (the most qualified). 'The post of director' uses 'the' because it is a single, specific position — Option D's 'a post' wrongly renders an identified role as one among many unknowns.

questions.stem: Choose the correct articles: 'I developed ___ keen interest in ___ economics after reading ___ book on ___ history of capitalism.'

options.option_text: a keen interest, the economics, a book, the history
a keen interest, economics, a book, the history
the keen interest, economics, a book, the history
a keen interest, economics, the book, the history

questions.explanation: 'A keen interest' correctly uses the indefinite article for a general feeling. Academic disciplines (economics, physics, mathematics) take zero article when used generically — Option A's 'the economics' is a common exam-setter trap. 'A book' is correct as first mention; 'the history of capitalism' requires 'the' because the postmodifier 'of capitalism' specifies a particular, bounded history. Option D wrongly uses 'the book' without prior contextual reference.
